name: accessibility
title: Control Accessibility
description: Check or control accessibility services. On Android: omit talkback to check TalkBack state, or pass talkback: true/false to enable/disable it. On iOS: omit voiceover to check VoiceOver state, or pass voiceover: true/false to enable/disable it (Simulator via simctl, physical devices via the Settings app). After enabling TalkBack, reports a blocking system runtime permission prompt in warning and blockingPrompt when detected; AutoMobile does not dismiss it. Use observe, then tapOn to answer the prompt. Always returns fresh state from the device, regardless of feature flags: enabled is what the device reports. When force-accessibility-mode or accessibility-auto-detect: off changes what the action tools assume, detectionOverride names it ({ mode: forced-on | auto-detect-off, effectiveEnabled }); it is absent otherwise.

talkback.description: Enable (true) or disable (false) TalkBack on the active Android device

name: accessibilityAction

Target the element by resourceId, text or contentDesc; it needs a unique resource-id. An action the element does not offer is refused, and the error lists the actions it does offer (custom ones as custom:<label>).

name: accessibilityAudit
title: Audit Native Accessibility
description: Run the platform's own accessibility audit engine on the current screen. iOS (iOS 17+, Simulator and physical) runs XCUITest performAccessibilityAudit and reports contrast, hitRegion, dynamicType, textClipped, sufficientDescription, trait and elementDetection issues, each with the element's accessibility identifier as elementId (usable with tapOn/highlight) and bounds. Unlike the host-side WCAG audit, the platform engine sees real hit regions, Dynamic Type support and clipped text. Android (Accessibility Test Framework) is not available yet and returns errorCode unsupported_platform; a runner that predates this command returns errorCode unsupported_capability.

name: displayConfig
title: Configure Display
description: Read or set the visual display configuration — font/text scale, effective display density, light/dark (night mode) theme, and on Android the runtime screen size, navigation mode (gesture / 3-button / 2-button) and display-cutout emulation — for adaptive-layout, edge-to-edge and large-font accessibility testing. A call with no set field reads current values; providing fontScale, density, theme, size, navigationMode, displayCutout, or reset applies the change and returns applied + previous values so the client can restore. Android supports all three fields (density overrides are best-effort on physical devices); iOS supports theme (the Simulator via `simctl ui appearance`, physical devices through the CtrlProxy runner) and, on the Simulator only, font scale as a Dynamic Type category (via `simctl ui content_size`; fontScale maps to the nearest category and contentSize selects one exactly; reads report both). Android size, navigationMode and displayCutout use `wm size` and the system image's overlays; values the image does not ship are refused and `available` lists the ones it has; size, overlay and density changes invalidate cached observations and coordinates. On Android, reset restores font scale, density and screen size to device defaults, navigation mode and display cutout to the values recorded before they were first changed, and night mode only to the value displayConfig replaced earlier in this process; otherwise night mode is left unchanged. Releasing or rebinding the session that changed size, navigationMode or displayCutout restores them through the same record as displayProfile; sessionless changes persist until reset. Android reset never forces light mode. iOS Simulator reset restores light appearance and the content size category displayConfig replaced earlier in this process; physical iOS reset restores the appearance displayConfig first replaced there (light if none). The accessibility display preferences increaseContrast, reduceMotion and boldText are read and set on Android and the iOS Simulator, and colorInversion, colorCorrection, magnification, magnificationScale and extraDim (API 31+) on Android; `supported` reports each as true (proven by read-back), partial (stored setting reads back but running apps must relaunch; reason in supportNotes) or false, and reset restores the ones displayConfig changed. reset: "factory" additionally forces platform defaults (light theme, iOS content size large, accessibility display preferences off) regardless of recorded baselines, including after a daemon restart.

fontScale.description: System text scale, or 'default' to remove Android's explicit override and restore its inherited default. On the iOS Simulator, selects the nearest Dynamic Type category (1 = large; 'default' = large). Omit to leave unchanged.

contentSize.description: iOS Simulator only: an exact Dynamic Type category for `simctl ui content_size`, instead of the nearest one to fontScale. Cannot be combined with fontScale. Omit to leave unchanged.

density.description: Effective display density: an explicit dpi (e.g. 480), or a relative bucket (smaller/default/larger). Numeric values must be 72-1280 dpi. Android only; best-effort on physical devices. Omit to leave unchanged.

theme.description: Light, dark, system (follow-device), or custom (Android user-defined night-mode schedule) theme / night mode. Supported on Android; the iOS Simulator supports only 'light'/'dark'. 'custom' mainly exists to restore a device previously on a custom schedule (from an earlier call's `previous.theme`). Omit to leave unchanged.

size.description: Android: override the screen size in pixels, natural orientation (`wm size WxH`), or 'default' to remove the override. Each side must be 200 px to twice the physical size. Best-effort on physical devices. Omit to leave unchanged.

navigationMode.description: Android: gesture, threeButton or twoButton navigation via the system image's navbar overlay (`cmd overlay enable-exclusive --category`); 'default' disables every navbar overlay. Values the image does not ship are refused; read `available`. Omit to leave unchanged.

displayCutout.description: Android: emulate a display cutout via the system image's cutout-emulation overlay, or 'none' to disable it. Values the image does not ship are refused; read `available`. Omit to leave unchanged.

display.description: Android panel key, role, or active that size reads and sets; the default display when omitted. navigationMode and displayCutout are device-wide.

increaseContrast.description: Increase Contrast. Android: high-contrast text (secure high_text_contrast_enabled). iOS Simulator: `simctl ui increase_contrast`. Omit to leave unchanged.

reduceMotion.description: Reduce Motion. Android: Remove animations (all three animation scales 0; false restores the scales replaced earlier, else 1). iOS Simulator: partial, written to com.apple.Accessibility defaults; relaunch the app to observe. Omit to leave unchanged.

boldText.description: Bold Text. Android API 31+: secure font_weight_adjustment 300. iOS Simulator: partial, written to com.apple.Accessibility defaults; relaunch the app to observe. Omit to leave unchanged.

colorCorrection.description: Android: color correction (daltonizer) mode, or 'off'. 'grayscale' is monochromacy.

magnification.description: Android: enable the triple-tap magnification gesture. Enabling it does not zoom the screen until the gesture is performed.

magnificationScale.description: Android: the magnification gesture's zoom factor (AOSP default 2).

reset.description: Pass "factory" to restore platform defaults no matter which baselines were recorded, including after a daemon restart or for changes made outside a session: light theme, iOS content size large, accessibility display preferences off, font scale 1.0, density and size defaults. Pass true for the baseline-only reset described next. On Android, restore font scale, density and screen size to device defaults, and navigation mode and display cutout to the values recorded before they were first changed. Restore night mode only to the value displayConfig replaced earlier in this process; otherwise leave it unchanged. Android reset never forces light mode. On the iOS Simulator, reset restores light appearance and the content size category displayConfig replaced earlier in this process. On both, restore each accessibility display preference that displayConfig changed earlier in this process.

name: getDeviceState
title: Get Device State
description: Read device-level state including clock (Android epoch-second instant and automaticTime, readable without root; unsupported on iOS), Do Not Disturb, the connectivity toggles (airplaneMode, wifiEnabled, bluetoothEnabled, locationEnabled), iOS Simulator biometric enrollment, network condition (device-wide on Android; on an iOS Simulator the per-app offline rules the network filter enforces, with revision and lease), and Android emulator virtual sensor values (sensors: acceleration, gyroscope, magnetic-field, orientation, temperature, proximity, light, pressure, humidity via `emu sensor get`, with unavailable listing sensors the AVD refuses; change them with setSensor). Use it as the idempotency oracle before flipping a toggle — a bare call returns doNotDisturb + connectivity, so you can check whether Airplane mode is already on instead of inferring it from the status bar. Each connectivity field is true/false, or omitted when the device could not answer (the key is absent on this API level, or the value did not parse) — omitted never means off. Android only: iOS reports connectivity unsupported, because Airplane mode / Wi-Fi / Bluetooth / Location have no simctl or devicectl read verb and a simulator shares the host's network stack. screenLock (Android) reports the lock credential type (none, pin, password, pattern, or unknown) and whether it is secure, never the credential. Clock control supports only rootable Android emulators; Play Store images, physical devices and iOS return unsupported. Set accepts ISO-8601 instants within 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z .. 2100-01-01T00:00:00Z (inclusive); cumulative advance must stay in that window. Commands have second-level precision; advance requires integer byMs >= 1000 (maximum 315360000000), uses device read-back time, and verifies movement with a 2000ms tolerance; set within tolerance reports outcome=unchanged. On session release/rebind/teardown/reset, AutoMobile explicitly restores HOST-derived real time plus the original auto_time, even if it was 1, and verifies both. Failed restore is retried and quarantines the device until success or removal. Clock control restarts adbd on the emulator; connections such as port forwards may be re-established. Restore unroots adbd if AutoMobile rooted it (bounded, best-effort). Hierarchy/observe caches and freshness baselines are invalidated on every clock change. The restore slot is in memory only: daemon restart loses it; reset is recovery to HOST time plus auto_time=1 on a rootable emulator. Without a slot, unsupported targets report unsupported/nothing to reset without clock mutations; with a slot, refused root reports failure and retains pending restoration. Sessionless callers must reset explicitly. Session-bound and sessionless clock writes share one device queue and original ownership baseline; session release restores the device while sessionless ownership persists until reset or removal. Removal cancels clock work for that device incarnation. Changing the clock affects TLS/certificate validation, token expiry, and freshness checks.

name: injectAudioInput
title: Inject Emulator Microphone Audio
description: Play a WAV file or a built-in tone into an Android emulator's or iOS Simulator's microphone, so an app under test records known audio (voice notes, voice search, calls). An emulator streams through its own gRPC audio API, isolated per emulator. A simulator goes through the host's loopback input device, which every simulator on the host shares, so one simulator injection runs per host. For Android, AutoMobile opens and verifies a guest microphone capture before streaming and closes its recorder when injection ends. Returns an injectionId once streaming starts; stop it with stopAudioInput. Session release stops it. Errors lead with a code: [audio_injection_busy] another injection holds the microphone; [audio_injection_unsupported] no route (not a local emulator with gRPC audio, or a host without a loopback default input); [audio_loopback_failed] the host loopback helper failed; [audio_guest_capture_unavailable] a safe Android guest capture could not be verified; [audio_emulator_exited] the emulator exited during injection. Physical devices are refused.

force.description: Drop every AVD-name comparison on the way to the kill -- the emulator-console probe that confirms which AVD is running on this serial, and the platform kill's own check against a fresh discovery -- and act on whatever occupies the serial. Use only when the console has wedged and the normal call refuses because the AVD name cannot be confirmed. This does not override the conflict check, it removes it: force means 'act on whatever emulator currently occupies this serial', including a different AVD that took the serial over. It does NOT select a different serial, and a serial with nothing running on it still refuses. Nor does it override the refusal raised when this daemon's pool entry for the serial was retired and replaced while the action was being prepared, or deleteDevice's refusal to delete a stopped image while a booted emulator that cannot be identified at all is attached. Android emulators only; accepted and ignored for iOS and physical devices. Separately, on any platform, force also stops a device another session holds, which is otherwise refused.

name: killProfile

Each profile reports its evidence status and each step applied | unsupported | failed. apply is idempotent and records the state before the first change; reset restores it, and in a daemon session release or rebind does too. list shows the catalog and the OEM behaviour that cannot be simulated. Simulates effects, not firmware.

name: prototype
title: Manage UI Prototype
description: shared:{key,as:"element"|"bounds"} requires prototype_shared_element_v2; sharedKey remains the v1 bounds alias; do not set both. Repeat shared.key templates need repeat.key and must reference that field. Shared pairs cannot cross dialog or bottomSheet boundaries. style.shadows, style.cornerStyle, style.border.gradient, scroll.fadeEdges and image.filter require prototype_style_polish_v2. testSessionBegin (id, goal?, cohort?), testSessionEnd (id) and testSessionReport (id or testSessionId) record and report host-local user-testing sessions without a device request. Reports include screen funnels, time, validation failures and dead taps; text values are never stored. Show with window.deadTaps:true (prototype_dead_tap_v1) to enable dead taps. Show (always a full spec, inline as spec or from a local JSON file as specPath), patch (id and ops), dismiss (id or all:true), status (host-local, no device request), screenMap (host-only: spec or specPath in, {screenMap:{nodes,edges},mermaid} out; stack screens, pager pages, sheets and dialogs with the push/replace/pop/popToRoot/setPage actions between them), inspect (asks the device which prototypes it is showing and adopts them into status and awaitEvent; use it after a session release or reconnect), or awaitEvent for a prototype id on Android, or on an iOS simulator through the prototype agent that launchApp with prototype:true injects (show, patch, dismiss, status, inspect, awaitEvent; sizes are points). save (spec/assets/label/icon), listSaved and deleteSaved (id) need prototype_saved_v1 on Android, or an iOS simulator (no agent needed) using the verified viewer template (or AUTOMOBILE_IOS_PROTOTYPE_VIEWER) for save; icon is an asset uploaded in the same call. On Android, save with pin:true then asks the launcher to pin a shortcut (pinned: pinned|pending|unsupported; pending until the launcher dialog is accepted (autoConfirm taps it), declining sends nothing). After a pin or shortcut update the host looks for the shortcut on the home screen and, if it is missing, restarts the default launcher once (launcherRestarted, shortcutVisible); restartLauncher:false opts out. deleteSaved disables the shortcut, and removeIcon:true clears it with adb only when no saved prototype remains. iOS installs an app icon on the home screen and ignores pin. iOS listSaved ids are bundle ids accepted by deleteSaved and omit savedAt. On Android or an iOS simulator with the ProtoViewer app installed, save without pin or icon imports the spec and its assets into the ProtoViewer library instead of the platform save path, and returns viewer {app, libraryId, label} plus a warning: ProtoViewer marks the entry imported, keeps its requests off until the user allows network in ProtoViewer, and does not attach it to this host (no awaitEvent, patch or inspect). If ProtoViewer is absent, older than this route, or its inbox is unusable, save keeps the platform save path. Each such save is a new library entry that listSaved and deleteSaved do not see. open with id set to that libraryId launches it on Android or an iOS simulator; open needs ProtoViewer installed. A show with the id of the prototype already on screen replaces it in place: it keeps the display and each pager's page (clamped), while the new spec's state is authoritative (values the user changed by tapping are not carried over unless the spec includes them); reset:true starts fresh instead. patch changes the prototype already on screen without re-sending the spec: {action:"patch",id,ops:[...]} with ops add/replace/remove/test on /data (content, agent-owned) or /state/<key> (needs baseRevision; the device refuses with conflict if the user changed that key since), and replaceNode {id,node} for one node by id; use show for a new screen or a window, theme or root change. patch needs a device advertising prototype_patch_v1 and is refused otherwise: use show. To present alternatives, show one design, describe it and the others in chat (what each is, what changed, which you recommend), and show the next on request; or show one spec whose pager holds every design with a visible label per page. Ask the user in chat which they prefer; never wait on the device for a choice. awaitEvent returns one buffered event, supports eventName/kind and afterSequence, and times out successfully (timedOut:true); default 30000 ms, maximum 60000 ms. Input and state changes (text input, toggles, sliders etc.) arrive as kind emit with eventName change (there is no separate change kind), with payload {key,value} for one changed key or {keys,values} for severalBuffer: 64 events per session/device/id; overflow drops oldest and reports droppedCount. Lower-or-equal sequences are ignored, including late arrivals and reconnect replays. simulate with id and advanceTimeMs (integer 1..3600000) advances prototype timers without waiting and returns fired; it requires prototype_timers_v1. startTimer {id,afterMs,everyMs?,maxRuns?,actions} and cancelTimer {id} require that capability; inspect reports timers {id,nextFireInMs,runs}. Nodes: box/row/column/flow/grid/carousel, text/image/icon/spacer/textField/searchBar, Material switch/checkbox/button/radioGroup/listItem/slider/chip/card/iconButton/fab/segmentedButton/topAppBar/divider/badge/progress/chart/dialog/snackbar/timePicker/datePicker bound to state keys, scroll/pager/stack/tabBar/bottomNav/bottomSheet/tooltip/drawer/adaptive; actions: emit/setPage/push/pop/popToRoot/replace/setState/toggle/increment/decrement/dismiss/setData/appendData/prependData/removeData/request. Stack {type:"stack",id,start,screens} needs prototype_stack_v1; only its top screen renders, and status/inspect report stacks {id:{path,depth}}. screen_changed has name = stack id and payload {screen,depth}. Reuse: a top-level components:{name:{root}} map placed with {type:"use",component,props} nodes, expanded on the host with {props.<field>} bound like repeat placeholders. Sizes and anchors use dp (points on iOS). A node's anchor {type:"element",selector:{elementId,text,testTag,container},alignment:cover|top|bottom|start|end,offset?} is resolved once at show against the app (the prototype excluded) and converted to dp with the display density (iOS bounds are already points); a missing, ambiguous or off-screen element fails the show, and the result reports anchors and hierarchyUpdatedAt (show again to re-anchor). {type:"bounds",bounds:{x,y,width,height}} is screen dp (screen points on iOS). Window placement: fullscreen/sheet/floating, window.opacity: 0-100 (default 100). window.chrome: none (default) or bar, fullscreen only: on a device advertising prototype_window_chrome_v1, none draws no host dismiss bar and fills the window including under the status bar (use safeAreaPadding on a top bar), and a two-finger long press (about 1 s) reveals a dismiss pill for 5 s; window.persistence: "device" defaults to bar. Without the capability the bar is kept, explicit none is refused, and lastResult.chrome says which was drawn. window.backdrop {material ultraThin|thin|regular|thick|glass, blur? 0-150 dp, tint? one hex or role} blurs what is behind the window and needs prototype_backdrop_v1 (refused without it); lastResult.backdrop is blur or fallback (a tonal fill where blur is unavailable). Example: {action:"show",spec:{id:"demo",window:{placement:{type:"fullscreen"},opacity:80},root:{type:"text",text:"Hello"}}}. show also accepts assets:[{id,path}] (absolute local PNG/JPEG/WebP file path, or a TTF/OTF font file referenced from style.fontFamily as {asset}, or an Android-only .agsl source referenced from style.shader as {asset,uniforms?}; AGSL needs AUTOMOBILE_PROTOTYPE_CUSTOM_SHADERS=1 and prototype_custom_shaders_v1 and is refused by iOS and ProtoViewer bundles) or [{id,observation}] (an observation screenshot URI) uploaded before the prototype is sent; image nodes reference the id. If the device reports supplied assets missing, they are re-uploaded and the prototype re-sent once; missingAssets and warning report what is still missing. Verify with observe; no screenshot is returned. A successful show or patch also returns accessibilityFindings, an advisory host-side lint (unlabeled controls, images and text fields, low text contrast in light and dark, tap targets under 48dp) with spec paths; it never refuses a show. On Android a session prototype is tied to the app it was shown over: while another app is in front it is hidden (state kept, no dismissed event, not in observe, layer "prototype" calls fail saying so) and it returns with the app; a device-persistent prototype is not tied to an app. Status makes no device request, marks a prototype suspended:true once an inspect finds it hidden that way (an awaitEvent that then times out warns), and includes pendingCount/lastSequence/droppedCount after events arrive. Device dismissed events remove shown status; the terminal event remains available until consumed or explicit show/dismiss. Awaiting consumes events; unmatched events remain buffered. Optional MCP progress reports wait start/finish without delaying the wait. Session release, device removal and unbinding clear buffers. A disconnect alone is not observed. window.layer: system (default, above system UI) or app (above apps only, so the shade, keyboard and screenshot preview draw over it; the daemon grants CtrlProxy SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW with appops first). window.persistence: session (default) or device: the prototype stays interactive after USB/adb disconnect and session end with no idle timeout, keeps its assets, and carries a visible Close control; remove it with that control, dismiss, or a new show. Both are Android only and need a CtrlProxy advertising prototype_window_options_v1. A device-persistent prototype keeps emitting taps, page changes and text input while no host is connected: the device buffers the last 200 events (oldest dropped, counted) and delivers them when a host connects or on inspect, with sequences continuing and no rewind; inspect returns deviceDroppedEvents. inspect needs a CtrlProxy advertising prototype_persistence_replay_v1 and is refused otherwise. On an iOS simulator inspect asks the agent (prototype_inspect_v1) for the one prototype it shows, with no suspended and no deviceDroppedEvents, and is refused with a relaunch hint on an older agent. Light and dark: show takes appearance device (default), light or dark, which pins what the system setting means for that show without changing the device; it replaces the system setting only (mode order: explicit theme.mode, then the flat theme.colors.background/surface luminance, then an opaque authored background, then appearance, else the device), and light or dark is refused unless the device advertises prototype_appearance_v1. Such a device reports appearance {mode, source, deviceDark} in the show result and per prototype in inspect; deviceDark (the device's own setting) appears only in those device answers. The host-local status reports mode and source only (kept current by appearance_changed events, which carry just mode and source), because the device can flip while a pinned mode stays put and then no event arrives; call inspect for the current deviceDark. It sends one appearance_changed event (match it with awaitEvent kind:"appearance_changed", not eventName: its name is null; payload {mode, source}) on any change of the resolved mode while shown (the device flipping, or prototype state changing an inferred mode), never for the show itself. If an appearance_changed event arrives while a show is in flight the host cannot order the two, so that status entry has no appearance until a later event or inspect states it. In a scrim slot only the scrim role gets alpha (0.4); other roles are drawn unchanged. row/listItem swipeActions {start?,end?,fullSwipe?} (1-3 {label,icon?,role?,color?,onTap} per side; not inside a horizontal pager or carousel) require prototype_swipe_actions_v1; revealed buttons are tagged <rowTag>.swipe.<index>. Flow/grid require prototype_flow_grid_v1; grid is non-lazy and never scrolls itself (wrap it in scroll). scroll.refresh {stateKey,onRefresh} (pull-to-refresh on a vertical scroll; stateKey is a boolean that shows the indicator) requires prototype_refresh_v1. carousel {itemWidth,variant?,itemSpacing?,children} (horizontal snapping row) and pager indicator "dots" require prototype_carousel_v1. Per-mode {light, dark} forms need prototype_theme_modes_v1. Stack {type:"stack",id,start,screens} requires prototype_stack_v1 and is refused otherwise. Data, repeat.items {path}, repeat.key, {data:/pointer} text and {data: pointer} conditions require prototype_data_model_v1. setData {path,value}, appendData {path,value}, prependData {path,value} and removeData {path} (path is /data/<pointer>, with a whole {index} segment inside a repeat; value is {value: json}, {state: key}, {data: pointer}, or {item: field}/{index: true} in a repeat) change /data from a tap and require prototype_data_actions_v1. Each device write is a change event (awaitEvent kind:"change") with name = the written /data path and payload {op, value?, revision}; once the device has written a prototype's data, a patch with /data ops needs baseRevision (the latest revision seen) and is refused with conflict {revision, state, data} if a newer write touched an overlapping path. request {url, method?, headers?, query?, body?, into?, statusKey?, via?, timeoutMs?, onSuccess?, onError?} calls any absolute http(s) URL from a tap (no host allowlist; url takes {key} and {data:/pointer} placeholders; headers/query values and body are literals or {state}/{data}/{value}/{item} bindings) and needs prototype_network_v1, plus prototype_network_device_v1 for via "device" (default via "host": the host makes the call). A 2xx body (JSON, else a string) is written to into (a /data path naming an object member) like setData, and {status, headers, durationMs, error?} to into + "__meta" (/data/feed -> /data/feed__meta); a non-2xx status or failure leaves into alone and sets meta.error. statusKey names a declared string state key that moves loading -> success|error, for visibleWhen; onSuccess/onError are action lists (nest up to 4 deep). A newer request to the same into cancels the older. Limits: timeoutMs max 30000 (default 10000), response 262144 bytes, 4 in flight per device. Each finished request is an emit event named prototype_request (payload {requestId, method, url, via, into?, outcome, status?, durationMs, error?}; await it with kind emit, eventName prototype_request). Input checks, validateOn, enabledWhen, {valid: key|keys} conditions and emit.requireValid require prototype_checks_v1; see the guide for checks and formats. textField options (label, variant, supportingText, keyboardType, secure, multiline, minLines, maxLines, maxLength) require prototype_text_field_options_v1; a device without it refuses the show. textField trailingIcon {icon,label,onTap?}, imeAction (done|next|search|send|go) and onSubmit require prototype_text_field_actions_v1 (not allowed with multiline). textField leadingIcon (icon name) requires prototype_text_field_leading_icon_v1. onLongPress/onDoubleTap on box/row/column/text/image/icon/card require prototype_gestures_v1. On Android, show replaceOthers:false retains other windows up to a limit of 4 (prototype_multi_surface_v1); a fifth is refused listing the shown ids. Read the MCP resource automobile:prototype for the authoring guide (repeat grammar, limits, theme roles); look up icon names with automobile:prototype/icons?query=<word>. Read automobile:prototype/native?id=<id> for the spec, assets and a Compose or SwiftUI host file that embed it in an app. tooltip requires prototype_tooltip_v1; drawer requires prototype_drawer_v1. searchBar requires prototype_search_bar_v1 for show and patch. State-key contains/startsWith/lengthGt/lengthLt conditions and textField errorWhen/errorText require prototype_string_conditions_v1. errorWhen forces error styling without changing checks-based validity. {data, empty} conditions and style shimmer require prototype_loading_states_v1. animate.tempo fast|default|slow requires prototype_motion_tokens_v1 (iOS 17+); tempo excludes durationMs and easing and uses contract springs by property role and spec motion scheme. animate, style scale/rotation, transition slideStart|slideEnd|scale and image zoomable require prototype_motion_v2. Keyframes: node keyframes {trigger: {key} or {data: pointer}, durationMs: 100-3000, tracks}; 2-8 [fraction,value] points per track, rest endpoints, 16 expanded nodes, prototype_keyframes_v1 (iOS 17+). Plays once on changes, skips mount; reduced retains alpha. Expressive motion, node press {scale?,alpha?}, and animate of border, cornerRadius, elevation, shadowColor, padding or dp width/height require prototype_motion_v3 (Android only). transition as {type, delayMs?} (0-600 ms) or blurReplace, and box/row/column stagger {ms 0-100, order? forward|reverse|center} (every child's total delay at most 600 ms), require prototype_choreography_v1. window.transition auto|none|fade|slide|scale and repeat.stagger (0-100 ms per instance, capped at 600 ms) require prototype_window_motion_v1 on Android. Text-only contentTransition numeric|crossfade|none (default none) requires prototype_content_transition_v1 unless none; numeric rolls changed digits by resolved value, spans crossfade; motion none snaps. icon.effect {type, trigger? | repeat?} requires prototype_icon_effects_v1: bounce|pulse|scale|variableColor|wiggle|rotate|breathe|replace|drawOn; trigger {key} or {data} replays per change, repeat is infinite or 1-20, mutually exclusive. String tables and {t:key|count} require prototype_strings_v1; show locale overrides device locales only for strings. Node semantics {heading,liveRegion,group,label,hint,traits} requires prototype_semantics_v1. list {repeat:{items:{path},as,key},children:[row],header?,footer?,axis?,spacing?,contentPadding?,onEndReached?,endThreshold?,refresh?,maxItems?} is a lazy scrolling collection requiring prototype_lazy_list_v1 and prototype_data_model_v1. Its row template counts once, supports up to 500 keyed data rows, and refresh needs a vertical list. prependData {path,value} inserts one row at the start and requires prototype_lazy_list_v1; maxItems trims from the end. request.append {from,to} extends an existing data array from a response array; maxItems trims oldest rows atomically. motion: "reduced" requires prototype_reduced_motion_v1; iOS Reduce Motion selects reduced, Android animator/transition scale 0 selects off. sharedKey requires prototype_shared_element_v1; visibility morphs require visibleWhen and exactly two non-nested nodes per key, while a zoom source key names exactly one node without visibleWhen. At most 16 keys, and no repeat templates. Full motion morphs shared bounds, reduced fades, none snaps. Stack transition platform|slide|fade|none (default platform) and optional push/replace transition overrides require prototype_stack_transitions_v1; sharedAxisX|sharedAxisY|fadeThrough|zoom and push/replace source require prototype_stack_patterns_v1. Zoom needs source naming exactly one sharedKey node; Android substitutes fadeThrough and iOS substitutes platform push; pop/popToRoot take no override. Stack transition controls screen navigation, not its own visibleWhen. chart (line/area/bar/ring over /data arrays) requires prototype_chart_v1; observe reports its summary. A root-level storage {version, keys:["state:<key>","data:<pointer>"]} block (up to 64 unique keys: each state key declared in state, each data pointer a member of /data, no overlapping pointers, at most 262144 stored bytes) makes the device save those values per prototype id after every write (user edit, device data action, request response) and requires prototype_storage_v1. Precedence on the next show of the same id: stored values replace the spec's for the listed keys; a changed storage.version discards them all; a stored key no longer listed (or a show without storage) is dropped; a stored value that no longer fits (state type changed, data of another JSON kind, unwritable pointer) is dropped and the spec's value stands. A host patch to a stored key wins under the usual baseRevision rules and the device then stores it. inspect reports storage {version, keys:[{key,bytes}], totalBytes, skippedKeys?} per prototype (absent if the device does not report it); {action:"clearStorage",id} wipes an id's stored values (result cleared = keys removed) and is refused without prototype_storage_v1; deleteSaved also clears them. Mock backends (no server code): defineBackend {backendId, backend:{collections?, routes?, faults?, latencyMs?, seed?}} registers an in-process REST backend for this daemon session; a request action to https://<backendId>.mock.automobile.invalid/<path> with via "host" is answered by it, with no network, DNS or egress policy. Collections are json-server style (GET /<name> with ?field=value, q, _sort, _page/_limit, after/size; GET/POST/PATCH/PUT/DELETE /<name>/:id; every item needs an id); routes are canned {method,path:"/feed/:id",status?,headers?,body?,delayMs?} with {params.x}, {query.x} and {body:/pointer} placeholders; faults fail every nth or a seeded fraction of matching requests; backendLog {backendId, since?} returns the requests answered; clearBackend {backendId} removes it. show also takes mock ({backendId: definition}) or mockPath (an absolute JSON file of the same) to define backends before the spec is sent. Platform features (clipboard, share, haptics, sound, realtime channels, device state) use a root requires, the platform action and platform.on handlers; the Platform features guide section lists every module, call and event.

goal.description: testSessionBegin only: screen label such as checkout/done; reaching it completes the session

cohort.description: testSessionBegin only: free label echoed in the report; no cross-session aggregation

backendId.description: defineBackend, clearBackend and backendLog: the mock backend id; requests to https://<backendId>.mock.automobile.invalid are answered by it

backend.description: defineBackend only: {collections?:{name:[items with id]}, routes?:[{method,path,status?,headers?,body?,delayMs?}], faults?:[{path,method?,status,every|rate}], latencyMs?:{min,max}, seed?}. Replaces the backend of that id

mock.description: show only: mock backends to define before the spec is sent, as {backendId: definition} (the defineBackend definition shape); replaces any backend of the same id. Use with request actions to https://<backendId>.mock.automobile.invalid. Not allowed with mockPath

mockPath.description: show only: instead of mock, an absolute path of a local JSON file holding the same {backendId: definition} object (up to 2097152 bytes), read by the daemon; the path is never sent to the device

since.description: backendLog only: return requests with a sequence number above this

testSessionId.description: testSessionReport: stored session id, instead of the latest session for id

spec.description: style.shadows, style.cornerStyle, style.border.gradient, scroll.fadeEdges and image.filter require prototype_style_polish_v2. Full prototype spec: id, window, optional theme (design material|platform, default platform; explicit platform requires prototype_design_platform_v1; mode light|dark|system, colors.seed hex or colors.source "device", plus optional per-role hex overrides in colors such as colors.primary or colors.surface applied over that scheme in light and dark, typography.scale 0.75-1.5 and fontFamily sans|serif|mono, shapes.corner none|small|medium|large|full; text style.textStyle names a Material type role such as titleLarge; style color, background and border.color take hex or a Material colour role such as primary, onSurface, surfaceContainer; style.cornerRadius takes dp, none|extraSmall|small|medium|large|extraLarge|full, or per-corner {topStart,topEnd,bottomEnd,bottomStart} dp), optional state, root. window.opacity is 0-100, default 100. window.chrome: none (default) or bar, fullscreen only: on a device advertising prototype_window_chrome_v1, none draws no host dismiss bar and fills the window including under the status bar (use safeAreaPadding on a top bar), and a two-finger long press (about 1 s) reveals a dismiss pill for 5 s; window.persistence: "device" defaults to bar. Stack {type:"stack",id,start,screens} requires prototype_stack_v1 and is refused otherwise. Data, repeat.items {path}, repeat.key, {data:/pointer} text and {data: pointer} conditions require prototype_data_model_v1. onLongPress/onDoubleTap on box/row/column/text/image/icon/card require prototype_gestures_v1. searchBar requires prototype_search_bar_v1 for show and patch. Repeat shared.key templates need repeat.key and must reference that field. Shared pairs cannot cross dialog or bottomSheet boundaries.  keyed data rows, and refresh needs a vertical list. prependData {path,value} inserts one row at the start and requires prototype_lazy_list_v1; maxItems trims from the end. request.append {from,to} extends an existing data array from a response array; maxItems trims oldest rows atomically. String tables and {t:key|count} require prototype_strings_v1; show locale overrides device locales only for strings. Node semantics {heading,liveRegion,group,label,hint,traits} requires prototype_semantics_v1. motion: "reduced" requires prototype_reduced_motion_v1; iOS Reduce Motion selects reduced, Android animator/transition scale 0 selects off. sharedKey requires prototype_shared_element_v1; visibility morphs require visibleWhen and exactly two non-nested nodes per key, while a zoom source key names exactly one node without visibleWhen. effect.description: Icon animation. trigger {key} or {data} replays on value changes; repeat is infinite or 1-20. trigger and repeat are mutually exclusive; omit both for one play on appearance. replace follows name changes.

anyOf.description: Replaced on the host by components[component].root with {props.<field>} bound in the fields repeat binds; a placeholder that is the whole value keeps the prop's type

material.description: Frosted material behind the window: ultraThin, thin, regular, thick, or glass (Liquid Glass on iOS 26+; the fallback dim elsewhere)

blur.description: Blur radius in dp (points on iOS), 0-150; absent uses the material's own radius

tint.description: One colour (hex or Material role, not a per-mode pair) laid over the blur, and the solid fallback where blur is unavailable

backdrop.description: Blur what is behind the window (needs prototype_backdrop_v1). The show result reports backdrop blur or fallback; fallback is a tonal fill (tint at 85% alpha, else the surfaceContainer role at 85%) where blur is unavailable

chrome.description: Fullscreen only: none (default on a device advertising prototype_window_chrome_v1) removes the host dismiss bar; a two-finger long press (about 1 s) reveals a dismiss pill for 5 s. Device persistence defaults to bar. An older device keeps the bar and refuses explicit none; lastResult.chrome reports what it draws

keepScreenOn.description: Keep the screen awake while shown; needs prototype_platform_window_controls_v1

brightness.description: Screen brightness 0-100 for the prototype window while shown, or system; needs prototype_platform_window_controls_v1

orientation.description: Requested orientation while shown (best effort over an overlay); needs prototype_platform_window_controls_v1

statusBar.description: Status bar content style while shown (best effort where the runtime does not own the status bar); needs prototype_platform_window_controls_v1

layer.description: system (default): above system UI. app: just above apps, so the shade, keyboard and screenshot preview draw over it; needs SYSTEM_ALERT_WINDOW, granted with appops at show time; some system apps (for example Settings) hide app-layer prototypes; the show result then carries visible: false

persistence.description: session (default): dismissed when the last host client disconnects or after the idle timeout. device: stays interactive after USB/adb disconnect and session end, with no idle timeout, until its close control, an explicit dismiss, a replacing show, or the CtrlProxy service stops

email.description: Reserved domain only: example.test, example.com or *.invalid

auth.description: Fake sign-in accounts for auth.signIn (prototype_platform_auth_v1); unique ids, no passwords or tokens

location.description: Foreground location updates for /platform/location/current (prototype_platform_location_v1); needs location in requires.platform and requires.permissions

notifications.description: Notification channels for notifications.post (prototype_platform_notifications_v1); unique ids

components.description: Reusable node templates by name, placed with {type:"use",component,props}; expanded on the host before validation (use nesting up to 8 deep, no cycles, every prop used); limits apply to the expanded spec

ops.description: patch only: 1–64 ordered ops on /data, /state/<key>, or replaceNode {id,node}; validated atomically before sending

baseRevision.description: patch only: required for /state ops, and for /data ops once the device has written the prototype's data with setData/appendData/removeData; the patch is refused with conflict if a touched key or an overlapping /data path changed since this revision

specPath.description: show only: instead of spec, an absolute path of a local JSON file holding the same spec (up to 1048576 bytes) that the daemon reads and validates like an inline spec; the path is never sent to the device. Exactly one of spec or specPath. Use it for a spec a script generated, instead of pasting the JSON into the call.

display.description: show only: panel key, role, or active to show the prototype on. Precedence: explicit display, then the session display pin, then the default display. Needs a CtrlProxy advertising prototype_display_id_v2; a disconnected panel is refused. Ignored, with a warning, by a same-id show without reset, which keeps the display the prototype is on.

replaceOthers.description: show only: true (default) replaces other prototypes; false adds this prototype as another window (max 4 on screen; a fifth is refused listing the ones shown). A same-id show replaces only that prototype when false. Needs an Android device advertising prototype_multi_surface_v1; iOS shows one prototype at a time.

locale.description: show only: locale override for strings (prototype_strings_v1). Each show states it afresh; omitted uses the device preferred locales and re-resolves live. Forwarded only when spec has strings; missing translations return strings.fallback platformNotes.

pseudoLocale.description: show only: true sends a pseudo-localized copy of the spec: every string-table value/plural form, semantics label/hint, text, label, placeholder, headline, title and span is accented and padded by about 40%, wrapped in [ ], with {bindings} and {t:key|count} references left intact, so truncation and clipping show without a translation. The authored spec, status and patch base are unchanged; patch ops apply to the device copy. Each show states it afresh.

reset.description: show only: when the prototype with spec.id is already shown, start it fresh (pager pages from the spec, display re-resolved) instead of replacing it in place

appearance.description: show only: what the system light/dark setting means for this prototype. device (default) follows the device; light or dark pins it without changing the device or the app behind, so a spec with theme.mode "system" or no mode can be checked in both modes. It replaces the system setting only: an explicit theme.mode, a flat theme.colors.background/surface override and an opaque authored background still decide first. Each show states it afresh (a same-id show without it follows the device again). light and dark need a device advertising prototype_appearance_v1 and are refused otherwise.

advanceTimeMs.description: simulate only: advance the prototype clock without waiting

id.description: Prototype id required for dismiss (unless all: true), awaitEvent, deleteSaved and clearStorage; for open, the ProtoViewer library id (viewer.libraryId) a save returned

assets.description: show or save only: images to upload before the prototype is sent, as {id, path} with an absolute local file path or {id, observation} with an observation screenshot URI (PNG, JPEG or WebP, up to 4 MiB each, 16 MiB total, 32 assets). Reference each id from image nodes, or from style.fontFamily as {asset} for a TTF/OTF font file (path only, up to 2 MiB). Uploads are sequential; any failure fails the call before the prototype changes and names the assets already stored. If the device reports a supplied asset missing after the prototype is sent, it is re-uploaded and the prototype re-sent once.

id.description: Opaque asset id that spec image nodes reference (image.asset, or style.fontFamily {asset})

path.description: Absolute path the daemon can read: PNG/JPEG/WebP, a TTF/OTF font (2 MiB), or Android-only AGSL .agsl source (16 KiB; AUTOMOBILE_PROTOTYPE_CUSTOM_SHADERS=1 and prototype_custom_shaders_v1 required)

observation.description: Instead of path: an observation screenshot URI, automobile:observation/{deviceId}/{observationId}/screenshot (the observationScreenshotResourceUri that observe returns); it must still be that device's current observation

label.description: save only: label, defaults to spec.id; ProtoViewer takes one line without control or direction-override characters

icon.description: save only: icon asset id uploaded in assets in this call

pin.description: save only (Android): after saving, request a home-screen shortcut; the launcher then asks the user to confirm

autoConfirm.description: save only: requires pin; accepts the launcher dialog, verifies the pin

restartLauncher.description: save only (Android): false skips the automatic default-launcher restart that runs when a pinned or updated shortcut is not visible on the home screen

removeIcon.description: deleteSaved only (Android): clear CtrlProxy's shortcuts with adb when no saved prototype remains; otherwise a disabled icon remains

all.description: Dismiss all prototypes on the targeted device

eventName.description: awaitEvent only: filter event name; input and state changes use eventName change

kind.description: awaitEvent only: filter event kind. screen_changed (name = stack id, payload {screen, depth}) is sent only when the top screen or depth changes. page_changed (name = pager id, payload = the new zero-based page index) is sent when a pager settles on another page. appearance_changed (name null, payload {mode, source}) is sent once whenever the shown prototype's resolved light/dark mode changes, by a device advertising prototype_appearance_v1. Input and state changes (text input, toggles, sliders etc.) arrive as kind emit with eventName change (there is no separate change kind), with payload {key,value} for one changed key or {keys,values} for several. A finished request action arrives as kind emit with eventName prototype_request

afterSequence.description: awaitEvent only: return a sequence strictly above this cursor

timeoutMs.description: Device request timeout; awaitEvent defaults to 30000 ms, maximum 60000 ms; timeout is a successful empty result. save and open through ProtoViewer wait up to 15000 ms by default, maximum 60000 ms.

screenMap.description: screenMap only: the spec's screens and the actions that move between them

mermaid.description: screenMap only: the same map as a Mermaid flowchart

backend.description: defineBackend and clearBackend: the mock backend acted on

origin.description: Base URL a spec requests to reach this backend

cleared.description: clearBackend: false when no such backend existed

backendLog.description: backendLog: requests the backend answered, oldest first (latest 200 kept)

viewer.description: save and open on Android or an iOS simulator with ProtoViewer installed: the ProtoViewer library entry. The entry is imported: ProtoViewer sets its source, keeps its network off until the user allows it, and it is not attached to this host.

libraryId.description: Pass as id to open to launch this entry.

display.description: iOS multi-screen device (iPhone Duo): the panel the app was on when it answered. Absent on single-screen devices, older apps and ambiguous sizes.

id.description: Authored prototype id on Android; bundle id on iOS simulators, accepted by deleteSaved.

savedAt.description: Absent where the platform cannot report save time (iOS simulators).

launcherRestarted.description: Android save with pin: true when the default launcher was restarted to show the shortcut.

shortcutVisible.description: Android: whether the shortcut was seen on the home screen after a pin or update.

revision.description: patch only: current device revision after applying or refusing a patch

conflict.description: patch only: newer user edits or device /data writes that refused the whole patch, with current revision and touched state values or data paths

data.description: /data paths a newer device write (setData, appendData, prependData, removeData) touched

cleared.description: clearStorage only: how many stored keys the device removed (0 when nothing was stored); absent when the device did not say

stacks.description: Last reported stack paths and depths; absent when the device reports none

lastKnown.description: Pages, stacks and state are the last reported device snapshot, not a live device query

screenRound.description: Wear OS show only: whether the watch display is round, so content in the corners is clipped; absent on other devices or when unreadable

includeExtras.description: Opt in to raw accessibility extras metadata in structuredContent only (default off). Only meaningful with project:'full' or raw:true; text content always omits extras.

raw.description: Return the raw view hierarchy instead of the compact skeleton

project.description: Observation projection. 'skeleton' (default) returns a flat, actionable-only list (elementId/label/bounds/affordances) under `skeleton` in place of `viewHierarchy`; 'full' returns the raw view hierarchy under `viewHierarchy`. Each skeleton elementId/label is directly usable as a tapOn selector, except the collapsed keyboard row `<ime>` (drive it with sendKeys); re-request with raw/project:'full' to disambiguate.

skeleton.description: Always present alongside a diff (issue #6221 item 4.1): the same actionable-only selector surface a full observation's `skeleton` carries.

context.description: Non-actionable state-readout rows from the same projection as `skeleton` (issue #6221 item 1, #6256) — a timer countdown, a toggle's current-state text — present only when at least one such row survived. Populated alongside `skeleton` so a diff-mode response never silently drops the readout a client needs to tell a failed input from a successful one.

activeWindow.description: Same name/shape as a full observation's `activeWindow` (issue #6258): a diff-mode response otherwise carries no `activeWindow` at all, leaving a client no single accessor for 'what screen am I on' across full and diff modes. Populated from the post-transition observation, not by `diffObserveResult` itself.

freshness.description: Same name/shape as a full observation's `freshness` (issue #6258): a diff-mode response otherwise carries no `freshness` at all, leaving a client no single accessor for 'is this capture fresh' across full and diff modes. Populated from the post-transition observation, not by `diffObserveResult` itself.

screenSize.description: Same platform-native coordinate space as a full observation's `screenSize` and hierarchy/skeleton bounds; `units` identifies that space when present. Populated from the post-action observation, not by `diffObserveResult` itself.

truncationReasons.description: Why the captured hierarchy is incomplete (issue #6601) — the same field a full observation carries, so a client reads it the same way in both modes. In diff mode (issue #6933), any reason — host-cap (max_children[...]) or capture-fidelity (max_nodes, max_depth, max_children, cancelled) — may originate from either comparison input (baseline or current capture), so its presence means the comparison may be incomplete, not that this diff's own `skeleton`/`context` omit rows.

settled.description: Same name/meaning as a full observation's `settled` (issue #6866): whether the observation this diff was computed from passed the hierarchy-stability gate. Populated from the post-action observation, not by `diffObserveResult` itself, so a diff-mode client has the same accessor as a full-mode one.

settleMs.description: Same name/meaning as a full observation's `settleMs` (issue #9591), copied from the post-action observation.

settlePolls.description: Same name/meaning as a full observation's `settlePolls` (issue #9591), copied from the post-action observation.

accessibilityAuditSkipped.description: Same name/meaning as a full observation's `accessibilityAuditSkipped` (issue #6926): `settled_capture_adopted` means a settled capture replaced the action's original capture, so its audit was deliberately dropped rather than mismatched onto the returned hierarchy.

added.description: Absent on action-observation diffs: the diff's `skeleton` already lists every actionable node on the current screen (#11637).

removed.description: Absent on action-observation diffs: the diff's `skeleton` already lists every actionable node on the current screen (#11637).

key.description: INTERNAL positional identity key — see observeDiffNodeSchema.key. NOT a selector.

fromKey.description: The node's INTERNAL key on the baseline side, present only on content-identity re-pairs.

selector.description: Real, tapOn-usable selector for this diff entry, when one could be derived from its resource-id/view-id/text/content-desc — the same vocabulary skeleton rows use. Prefer this over `key` (issue #6221 item 4).

elementId.description: Android synthetic s2- ids are valid only for the observation that returned them; re-observe after the screen changes.

index.description: Replay disambiguator from the next observation's skeleton for a repeated elementId or id-less label. Omitted when the node is absent or its own group contains a promotable inert match. Unique selectors carry neither index nor ambiguous.

ambiguous.description: True when this selector matches multiple candidates, including inert nodes, and a safe replay index cannot be emitted. Never present with index or on a unique selector.

backend.description: iOS only, when the app registered an AutoMobile SDK observation bridge: sdk when its nodes were used, xctest when XCTest stood in.

fallbackReason.description: Why XCTest stood in for the bridge: it did not answer, or it does not support the action.

hierarchyServiceStarted.description: Present only when this session-less read started the hierarchy service on an unowned device.

truncationReasons.description: Per-window capture truncation codes (max_nodes, max_depth, max_children, cancelled, or newer APK codes). Absent or null when unavailable; complete windows omit reasons. Full/raw output keeps these here.

anyOf.description: Compact bounds tuple [left, top, right, bottom].

truncationReasons.description: Why the captured hierarchy is incomplete (issue #6601). Present only when rows were dropped — a device-side stop (max_nodes, max_depth, max_children, cancelled) or the host per-node child cap (max_children[<node> kept N of M]). This is the nested location `sanitizeObserveResult` leaves raw hierarchy reasons under `project:"full"` or `raw:true`; capture-fidelity reasons may also be lifted to the top-level `truncationReasons` field for skeleton/diff output, while a host-output max_children cap is not lifted to a non-diff skeleton.

Why the captured hierarchy is incomplete (issue #6601) — the same field a diff-mode observation carries, so a client reads it the same way in both modes. On this non-diff arm, it contains only capture-fidelity reasons (device-side max_nodes, max_depth, max_children, cancelled); its presence means `skeleton`/`context` omit rows. A host-output max_children[<node> kept N of M] cap trims only rendered `viewHierarchy` and is not lifted here.

settled.description: Whether this observation passed the hierarchy-stability gate (issue #6866): two consecutive structurally-equal captures. `false` means the bound expired, the action was not navigation-class, or the action failed — in every case the capture was never confirmed stable. Stamped on every embedded action observation.

settleMs.description: Milliseconds the hierarchy-stability gate spent re-observing (issue #9591). Present only when the gate ran. With `settled: false`, a value near the gate's budget means the screen kept changing or each read was slow; a value well below it means the gate stopped early.

settlePolls.description: Re-observations the hierarchy-stability gate took (issue #9591). Two are needed to settle; fewer at the budget means reads were too slow to compare.

accessibilityAuditSkipped.description: Why a requested accessibility audit was omitted from this observation (issue #6926): `settled_capture_adopted` means a settled capture replaced the action's original capture, so its audit was deliberately dropped rather than mismatched onto the returned hierarchy.

generation.description: Generation advances on notifyTransition calls for panel key, role, or posture changes, Android non-swap size changes and accepted pushed display_transition events (changed with a different panel key or non-swap size, added, removed, or device_state changes), iOS multi-panel rotation, and iOS setPosture hinge, observed identity, and settled notifications (potentially several increments per request), but not on captures, Android pure width/height swaps, or iOS same-observation geometry corrections. bounds.description: Bounds as the compact [left, top, right, bottom] tuple — always this shape for skeleton entries, in the same current-orientation native space as screenSize and tapAt.

occluded.description: Fully covered by the Android IME window or the visible iOS keyboard, or an iOS row with no visible tap area: off screen, under a navigation/status/tab bar, scrolled out of its scroll container, or covered by another control; this row has no actionable affordance.

selected.description: AutoMobile prototype rows only: the selected tab or option.

state.description: AutoMobile prototype rows only: the node's state description, e.g. Page 1 of 3.

enabled.description: Explicit disabled state on Android and iOS; omitted means enabled.

index.description: Disambiguator present when a replay-eligible row's elementId, or id-less label, repeats among other replay-eligible rows (issue #6221). __schema30.description: Compact bounds tuple [left, top, right, bottom], emitted in place of the {left, top, right, bottom} object.

key.description: INTERNAL positional identity key (NUL-delimited resource-id/bounds/text/sibling-index). attributes.description: This node's full raw attributes (including resource-id/view-id/text/content-desc — the real selector fields), so it can be reconstructed without the baseline.

__schema36.description: Element bounds. Default: positional tuple [left, top, right, bottom]; the object {left, top, right, bottom} (+ optional centerX/centerY) is also schema-valid. description: Android: send an explicit broadcast to the app under test (its package, or one of its receivers) with a typed intent (action, data, categories, typed extras), e.g. to toggle a debug flag or seed data. Reports the ordered-broadcast result; protected system broadcasts are refused with a typed error.

appId.description: Target package: the broadcast is always explicit to it

action.description: Broadcast action

waitForResult.description: Report the ordered-broadcast result code and data (default true)

name: sendKeys
title: Send Keyboard Input
description: Execute ordered typing, clear, raw-key, and semantic IME commands. Unicode: iOS any mode; Android a11y/ime/auto/eventAll/eventLast (event modes use a11y for unsupported runs). Android eventOnly/imeKeyEvents are ASCII-only. textLength counts code points.

display.description: Target panel key, role, or active

selector.description: Field to focus once before executing the ordered command sequence; supports nested container scope and unique selection

elementId.description: Resource ID, e.g. com.app:id/field

text.description: Text, content-desc, or placeholder of the field

textAny.description: Ordered text variants; first visible match wins

container.description: Nested container scope; outermost resolves first, each level searches strict descendants. Per-level index is zero-based. Requires a selector naming the field to focus.

selectionStrategy.description: Selection strategy: first (default), random, or unique. Unique requires exactly one match at every unindexed scope and target. Requires a selector naming the field to focus.

layer.description: app: exclude the AutoMobile prototype; prototype: prototype nodes only (error if none shown). Omit for both, topmost first

commands.description: One to 100 commands executed serially; execution stops on the first failure

text.description: Text to insert or replace; never echoed in the result

operation.description: Insert at the current selection (default) or replace the focused field

mode.description: Android delivery mode. Use ime, a11y, or auto for Unicode and emoji. auto uses the AutoMobile IME when supported, otherwise eventAll for insert or a11y for replace. ime commits complete graphemes; eventAll inserts whole graphemes and uses key events only for single printable ASCII characters. eventLast can split keycaps or decomposed letters. eventOnly and imeKeyEvents are ASCII-only; imeKeyEvents requires a compatible CtrlProxy APK and does not verify resulting editor text. iOS uses xcuiTypeText for every requested mode

keyboardProfile.description: Android keyboard behavior profile for this IME type call; restored afterward

key.description: Raw key or semantic IME key. Semantic next/previous/done/search/send/go ignore modifiers

modifiers.description: Raw-key modifier chord: shift, ctrl, alt, or meta (maximum 4 entries, including duplicates)

mode.description: Android clear delivery. auto (default) and ime clear through the AutoMobile IME, or key-event deletes on an older control-proxy APK or when the IME cannot be activated, so rich-text editors keep live formatting. a11y uses the accessibility set-text clear. iOS ignores this

includeExtras.description: Opt in to raw accessibility extras metadata in structuredContent only (default off). Only meaningful with project:'full' or raw:true; text content always omits extras.

raw.description: Return the raw view hierarchy instead of the compact skeleton

project.description: Observation projection. 'skeleton' (default) returns a flat, actionable-only list (elementId/label/bounds/affordances) under `skeleton` in place of `viewHierarchy`; 'full' returns the raw view hierarchy under `viewHierarchy`. Each skeleton elementId/label is directly usable as a tapOn selector, except the collapsed keyboard row `<ime>` (drive it with sendKeys); re-request with raw/project:'full' to disambiguate.

elementId.description: Container resource ID

name: sendSms
title: Simulate SMS
description: Send simulated incoming SMS: Android emulator, or a notification via the app's AutoMobile iOS SDK.

message.description: SMS body; max 1024 chars, no newlines/NUL

name: setActiveDevice
title: Set Active Device
description: Set active device using existing session binding or a sessionless per-MCP-connection device pin that lasts for that connection (cleared when the connection disconnects or the device is released). With a daemon session, display pins a display key or role (inner/cover/rear/external); null clears, omission preserves. Explicit display arguments (including active) bypass the pin; otherwise pin beats focus/posture. On single-display devices, active resolves to the sole key; on multi-display devices active cannot be pinned. all cannot be pinned. Missing or inactive pinned panels fail without dispatch; clear with display: null. Pins clear on release/rebind and are unsupported in direct mode. Returns a text JSON result with message, deviceId, optional sessionUuid, and displayPin (string or null) when display was passed or a pin is present/cleared; never-pinned calls omit displayPin.

display.description: Session display pin: display key or inner/cover/rear/external; null clears, omitted preserves. On single-display devices, active resolves to the sole key; on multi-display devices active cannot be pinned. all cannot be pinned. Requires a daemon session. JSON result displayPin reports the resulting selector or null after clearing; omitted for a never-pinned session.

name: setAppLinks
title: Set App Links
description: Android 12+: change an app's App Links state so https links open the app directly (or not). approve force-verifies autoVerify domains, leaving already-verified domains in non-settable states (system_configured, pre_verified, migrated, restored) untouched; reset clears them to none, reverify re-runs verification, userSelection enables/disables domains for a user, restore writes back the state recorded before the first change, or the closest shell-settable state with a note. Returns what changed, skipped domains, the per-domain state after, and a restore receipt; in a daemon session, release or rebind restores it. Read state with getDeepLinks.

appId.description: Android package name.

userId.description: Android user for userSelection and the read-back; defaults to the current user.

action.description: approve: force-approve autoVerify domains (pm set-app-links 2), leaving already-verified domains in non-settable states (system_configured, pre_verified, migrated, restored) untouched. reset: clear verification to none (pm set-app-links 0). reverify: ask the verifier again (asynchronous). userSelection: enable or disable domains for the user. restore: write back the state recorded before the first setAppLinks change, using the closest settable state when exact restoration is unavailable.

domains.description: approve, reset, userSelection: domains to change; omit for every declared domain.

enabled.description: userSelection only: true enables the domains for the user, false disables them.

name: setAppPermissions
title: Set Permissions
description: userId grant/revoke; device-wide reset ['all']; no POST_NOTIFICATIONS.

name: setDeviceResources
title: Set Device Resources
description: Set selected device resources and verify native state, including disabled iOS service impacts. All settings are opt-in; omitted resources stay unchanged. iOS Simulator services and Android optional apps/settings are runtime-dependent. Android changes return a restore receipt for exact restoration during the same boot. Disabling Google infrastructure changes push/auth behavior. Disabling calendarServices on a booted simulator is refused with code unsafe_device_resource_combination unless its service is not running. Request it when provisioning a new simulator so it applies before first boot, or leave it enabled. Preboot is unaffected; unsafeWith lists the applicable phases.

screenTime.description: Screen Time limits and usage tracking. Changes restriction behavior.

diagnosticReporting.description: Diagnostic collectors, feedback, location analytics, and call-quality reporting; reduces diagnostic evidence, not call transport.

siriAndAppIntents.description: iOS Simulator Siri requests, Shortcuts actions, and App Intents; excludes speech services and proactive suggestions.

icloudSettingsSync.description: iCloud system-settings synchronization and storage-plan recommendations; preserves accounts, credentials, CloudKit data, Drive, and Photos transfers.

messagingMaintenance.description: Apple Messages history cleanup, attachment transfer, and FaceTime message storage; preserves identity, message database XPC helpers, and system calling services.

mapsApp.description: Android Google Maps app; external navigation intents become unavailable.
