accessibilityApps.description: Optional Android accessibility apps. Active accessibility services are protected.

textToSpeech.description: Android Google speech synthesis; speech-dependent functionality becomes unavailable.

storeApp.description: Android Play Store app; installation, updates, billing and licensing may fail.

healthConnect.description: Android Health Connect controller and backup app; health integrations become unavailable.

adServices.description: Android AdServices API package; advertising/privacy APIs may fail. Does not remove mainline/APEX infrastructure.

onDevicePersonalization.description: Android on-device personalization service package; dependent APIs may fail.

wallpaperApps.description: Android wallpaper picker and optional live-wallpaper apps; changes wallpaper selection. Does not disable the shared wallpaper framework or widgets.

dialerApp.description: Optional Android dialer apps. Default role holders remain protected.

messagesApp.description: Optional Android SMS/Messages apps. Default role holders remain protected; excludes other apps' messaging.

googleServicesFramework.description: Android Google Services Framework; aggressive control that can break Google account and push integrations.

googlePlayServices.description: Android Google Play services; aggressive control that breaks dependent push, authentication, location and other integrations. Keep enabled for workflows that depend on those services.

icloudSync.description: Broad iCloud/account synchronization. Control is unsupported; use the narrower icloudSettingsSync setting.

restore.description: Restore exact prior Android overrides from a returned receipt. Requires the same boot and user. Specify resources or restore, never both.

timeoutMs.description: Total configuration budget in milliseconds. Defaults to 300000.

name: setDeviceState
title: Set Device State
description: Set device state such as Do Not Disturb, Android connectivity toggles (airplaneMode, wifiEnabled, bluetoothEnabled, locationEnabled), static location or background route playback on an Android emulator, iOS Simulator, or physical iOS device (through the CtrlProxy runner), iOS Simulator biometric enrollment, and device-wide network condition. A static fix, replacement route, or stop cancels the active route. The location result may include previousRoute with endedReason and lastError; stop also reports whether a route was active. On release or rebind of a session that set a location, iOS clears it (`simctl location clear` on a Simulator, the runner on a physical device); failed clears are retried and quarantine the device until success or removal. Android emulator fixes persist after the session because the emulator console has no unset command; reset the fix explicitly if needed. Direct-mode (sessionless) calls are unchanged; an existing session marker on the device also clears later sessionless fixes on release. cameraPoster sets or clears a virtual-scene back-camera poster (image path or generated QR, wall or table surface) on a running Android emulator through the emulator console, without a restart; it persists until cleared or the AVD is cold-booted, iOS and physical Android return unsupported, a console refusal (for example an AVD whose back camera is not virtualscene) is returned as an error, and the default camera pose may not face the poster. Connectivity values are desired end states and are verified by a fresh Android read; iOS connectivity writes are unsupported. Degraded network profiles (offline/veryBad/2g/3g/4g) are best-effort cellular shaping on an Android emulator, reported `partial` (they may not affect Wi-Fi/app traffic); only reset to `none` is fully verified. A session always restores the network to a clean `none` state on release/rebind. On an iOS Simulator networkCondition is per-app only: profile offline or none with appId, within a session, refuses the app's new connections through the opt-in network-extension filter under a renewed 15s lease; release, rebind, expiry or a missed renewal removes it, and other sessions cannot clear it. screenLock (Android) sets a PIN, password, or pattern with locksettings, or clears one (type none plus currentCredential); a session's own credential is cleared on its release (a failed clear is reported in the release result as screenLockRestore), an existing credential the session did not set is refused with errorCode lock_credential_preexisting, and the result reports only the type and outcome (for example set: true). The credential is redacted from logs, telemetry, and recorded plans; it is in the device's process list while locksettings runs. power (Android) fakes battery level/charger, battery saver, light or deep Doze (the tool unplugs the battery and turns the screen off first and reports those preconditions), app standby buckets and inactive state, Data Saver and thermal status, and returns a restoreReceipt of the values it replaced; a session restores them on release in reverse order and reports failures as powerRestore in the release result. Battery, Doze and thermal faking is refused on physical devices (power_physical_device_refused). Clock control supports only rootable Android emulators; Play Store images, physical devices and iOS return unsupported. Set accepts ISO-8601 instants within 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z .. 2100-01-01T00:00:00Z (inclusive); cumulative advance must stay in that window. Commands have second-level precision; advance requires integer byMs >= 1000 (maximum 315360000000), uses device read-back time, and verifies movement with a 2000ms tolerance; set within tolerance reports outcome=unchanged. On session release/rebind/teardown/reset, AutoMobile explicitly restores HOST-derived real time plus the original auto_time, even if it was 1, and verifies both. Failed restore is retried and quarantines the device until success or removal. Clock control restarts adbd on the emulator; connections such as port forwards may be re-established. Restore unroots adbd if AutoMobile rooted it (bounded, best-effort). Hierarchy/observe caches and freshness baselines are invalidated on every clock change. The restore slot is in memory only: daemon restart loses it; reset is recovery to HOST time plus auto_time=1 on a rootable emulator. Without a slot, unsupported targets report unsupported/nothing to reset without clock mutations; with a slot, refused root reports failure and retains pending restoration. Sessionless callers must reset explicitly. Session-bound and sessionless clock writes share one device queue and original ownership baseline; session release restores the device while sessionless ownership persists until reset or removal. Removal cancels clock work for that device incarnation. Changing the clock affects TLS/certificate validation, token expiry, and freshness checks.

doNotDisturb.description: Do Not Disturb state to apply.

enabled.description: Enable or disable Do Not Disturb

biometrics.description: iOS Simulator biometric enrollment state to apply.

enrollment.description: Set iOS Simulator biometric enrollment state.

airplaneMode.description: Enable or disable Airplane mode on Android.

wifiEnabled.description: Enable or disable Wi-Fi on Android.

bluetoothEnabled.description: Enable or disable Bluetooth on Android.

locationEnabled.description: Enable or disable Location on Android.

networkCondition.description: Network condition to apply: device-wide on an Android emulator, or offline/none for one app (appId) on an iOS Simulator.

profile.description: Device-wide network profile. Documented values: none=unshaped, offline=no data, veryBad≈GSM (550ms/14kbps), 2g≈EDGE (400ms/237kbps), 3g≈UMTS (200ms/1920kbps), 4g≈LTE. Degraded profiles are best-effort cellular shaping, reported `partial`, on Android emulators. iOS Simulator accepts only offline and none, for one app named by appId.

appId.description: iOS Simulator only, and required there: bundle id of the one app to take offline (profile=offline) or restore (profile=none). Its new connections are refused through AutoMobile's network filter; open connections continue. Needs a session.

cancel.description: Reset to normal connectivity (same as profile=none).

packetLossPercent.description: Documented target packet loss; the emulator console cannot enforce partial loss.

expiresInSeconds.description: TTL in seconds. When set on a degrading request, a timer resets the device to normal connectivity after it elapses, independent of session lifetime; session release/expiry also restores connectivity, whichever comes first. Capped at 2147483s (~24.8 days) to fit the timer's 32-bit limit.

clock.description: Set the real clock within 2000-01-01T00:00:00Z .. 2100-01-01T00:00:00Z, advance by integer byMs >= 1000 with second-level precision, or reset to host time and original auto_time (1 without a recorded slot). Rootable Android emulators only.

location.description: Set a static fix, start a timed route, or stop route playback on an Android emulator or iOS Simulator.

cameraPoster.description: Set (mode image or qr) or clear a virtual-scene back-camera poster on a RUNNING Android emulator via the emulator console, with no restart. surface defaults to wall. The AVD back camera must be virtualscene (see startDevice cameraPosterPath/cameraPosterQr). The console cannot confirm the poster is visible; the default camera pose may not face it.

path.description: Host PNG/JPG/JPEG path; must not contain whitespace.

text.description: Payload encoded into a generated QR poster.

screenLock.description: Android only. Set a secure lock-screen credential (type pin, password, or pattern as digits 1-9) with locksettings, or clear one with type none and currentCredential. A session clears the credential it set on release and reports a failed clear in the release result (screenLockRestore); a sessionless set is never cleared automatically. An existing credential this session did not set is never overwritten (errorCode lock_credential_preexisting). The credential is redacted from logs, telemetry and recorded plans, and never returned.

power.description: Android only. Fake power constraints: battery {level 0-100, charging ac|usb|wireless|none, reset}, batterySaver, doze off|light|deep (light/deep unplug the battery and turn the screen off first and report these as preconditions), standbyBucket {appId, bucket}, appInactive {appId, inactive}, dataSaver and thermalStatus 0-6 or reset. Battery, Doze and thermal faking is refused on physical devices (errorCode power_physical_device_refused); thermal override needs API 29+ and the restricted bucket API 30+ (errorCode power_unsupported_api_level). The result carries a restoreReceipt; a session restores every changed field in reverse order on release and reports failures in the release result (powerRestore). A sessionless change is never restored automatically.

charging.description: Fake charger source: ac, usb, wireless, or none (unplugged).

reset.description: true: return the battery to real values (`dumpsys battery reset`).

batterySaver.description: Turn battery saver on or off.

doze.description: Force light or deep Doze, or leave it (off). light/deep unplug the battery and turn the screen off first.

standbyBucket.description: Put an app in an App Standby bucket (restricted needs API 30+).

appInactive.description: Mark an app inactive (idle) or active.

dataSaver.description: Turn Data Saver (restrict background data) on or off.

thermalStatus.description: Override the thermal status 0 (none) to 6 (shutdown), or reset it (API 29+).

deviceCondition.description: Session-scoped root/integrity/fault test fixtures (behind the 'device-condition' feature flag). Every applied condition restores to a clean state on release, rebind or lease expiry. Send it in its own call, not combined with other setDeviceState fields.

rootState.description: Root fixture: 'rooted-detectable' plants inert su/busybox stubs and sets SELinux permissive so root-detection checks trip (Android, non-Play image, needs a writable /system); 'unset' restores.

integrityState.description: Integrity-signal state. Only 'unset' (clear) is available until an integrity injector lands.

battery.description: Battery fault via `dumpsys battery` (unplug / low 15% / full), or unset.

lowPower.description: Toggle `settings global low_power`, restored to its prior value, or unset.

doze.description: Force deep Doze via `dumpsys deviceidle force-idle`, or unset.

thermal.description: Override thermal status via `cmd thermalservice override-status`, or unset.

dontKeepActivities.description: Developer options 'Don't keep activities' via `settings global always_finish_activities`, restored to its prior value, or unset. Applies to activities left after the change.

storage.description: Use up free space on /data with a ballast file (`fallocate`): 'low' leaves about 128 MiB, 'full' about 8 MiB. Reset deletes the ballast. Or unset.

corruptAppFile.description: Damage one file in a debuggable app's data directory ({ package, path, mode }), e.g. a SQLite database or SharedPreferences XML. 'overwrite' zeroes its first 256 bytes, 'truncate' cuts it in half. Needs a debuggable app (run-as), force-stops the app, and keeps a copy that reset restores and verifies by checksum. Or unset.

revokePermission.description: Revoke one runtime permission from an installed app with `pm revoke` ({ package, permission }); reset re-grants it. Revoking kills the app's process, so it also restarts the app. Or unset.

disablePackage.description: Disable an installed app for the current user with `pm disable-user` ({ package }); reset runs `pm enable`. Or unset.

killApp.description: End an app's process once ({ package, mode }): 'background' is `am kill`, which only ends a process the system could reclaim and leaves the foreground app running; 'forceStop' is `am force-stop`, the user's Force stop. Nothing to reset; 'unset' is a no-op.

trimMemory.description: Send a running app an onTrimMemory level once ({ package, level }) with `am send-trim-memory`. The app must be running. Nothing to reset; 'unset' is a no-op.

clearPackageData.description: Clear an installed app's data with `pm clear` ({ package }). One-shot: it kills the app's process and cannot be undone, so there is nothing to reset. 'unset' is a no-op.

clockSkew.description: Set the device clock offsetSeconds ahead of (positive) or behind (negative) real time ({ offsetSeconds }), 3 seconds to 10 years either way, with automatic time off. Reset restores real time and the original automatic-time setting and verifies them. Rootable Android emulators only (needs adb root, which restarts adbd). Shares the device clock with setDeviceState.clock: a reset from either restores real time. Or unset.

faults.description: Power and lifecycle fault injectors (Android only, behind the feature flag).

motion.description: Vehicle motion on an Android Automotive emulator: 'parked' (gear park, speed 0, parking brake on) or 'driving' (gear drive, moving, brake off), set together so the state is consistent. Restored to the values read before the first change; or unset.

nightMode.description: Vehicle night-mode signal on an Android Automotive emulator, restored to its prior value; or unset.

vehicle.description: Vehicle state (Android Automotive emulators only; 'unsupported' elsewhere), via `cmd car_service inject-vhal-event`.

expiresInSeconds.description: Lease: restore every applied condition after this many seconds unless a later deviceCondition call renews it. Session-bound calls only.

reset.description: Restore every condition applied on this device and verify a clean read.

name: setKeyValue
title: Set Key Value
description: Set app key-value storage entry.

name.description: Storage name. iOS: empty string, "standard" (any case) or the app bundle id select the app's standard UserDefaults; any other value is a UserDefaults suite name (e.g. an app group) and must be a valid suite with no leading or trailing whitespace. Android: SharedPreferences file name without the .xml extension (letters, digits, underscore, dash, dot).

key.description: Key

userId.description: Android only: user whose copy of the app the direct-file (run-as) fallback edits (e.g. a work profile). Defaults to user 0 when the app is installed for it; otherwise to the one other running user that has it (an error asks for userId if several do). The SDK route is not user-scoped.

inputSchema.description: Provide either `name` (iOS UserDefaults suite / Android SharedPreferences name) or `fileName`

name: setNotificationPolicy
title: Set Notification Policy
description: Set app notification/DND policy state

name: setPosture
title: Set Posture
description: Set Android device posture or iPhone Duo simulator posture, with an optional Resizable Android display preset. Specify exactly one of posture or hingeAngle (finite degrees, 0-180 inclusive). Hinge angle is BEST EFFORT, emulator/simulator only, without displayPreset; unsupported returns status: unsupported with a reason and no state change. Android console support is detected at call time; iOS requires a runner advertising set_hinge_angle (#8547). Angle results echo hingeAngle and device posture read-back, or unknown with postureReason. Android strictly parses emu sensor get hinge-angle0 output as hinge-angle0 = <n>; iOS uses the runner angle. Both report observedHingeAngle when available and warn without failing when the resulting angle is unavailable or differs by more than 1 degree.

hingeAngle.description: Best effort hinge angle in degrees, 0-180 inclusive; specify exactly one of posture or hingeAngle. Emulator/simulator only; no displayPreset.

pinned.description: This call selected the panel using its session display pin.

generation.description: Generation advances on notifyTransition calls for panel key, role, or posture changes, Android non-swap size changes and accepted pushed display_transition events (changed with a different panel key or non-swap size, added, removed, or device_state changes), iOS multi-panel rotation, and iOS setPosture hinge, observed identity, and settled notifications (potentially several increments per request), but not on captures, Android pure width/height swaps, or iOS same-observation geometry corrections. Generation is comparable only within one session: it restarts at 0 when the device is released or the session ends, and on daemon restart.

name: setPreference
title: Set Preference
description: Write an Android system property, Android SharedPreferences key, or iOS UserDefaults key and return read-back verification. On iOS, appId is required and the store selector is suite (not name or fileName as on setKeyValue); omit suite or use Standard for the default store. Uses an already connected embedded AutoMobile SDK with storage inspection enabled; storage access itself never starts a runner. Reads can fall back to the simulator data container's on-disk plist, which may lag the running app. Writes use the container only when no SDK connection is open before sending; SDK write failures never trigger a second write. App-group suites require the connected SDK.

appId.description: App package or bundle id

suite.description: SharedPreferences file name or UserDefaults suite/app group

key.description: Preference key or Android system property name

userId.description: Android sharedPreferences only: user whose copy of the app to read/write (e.g. a work profile). Defaults to user 0 when the app is installed for it; otherwise to the one other running user that has it (an error asks for userId if several do). The result reports the userId used.

type.description: Value type for typed preference stores

name: setSensor
title: Set Emulator Sensor
description: Set or reset one Android emulator virtual sensor (acceleration, gyroscope, magnetic-field, orientation, temperature, proximity, light, pressure, humidity) through the emulator console. Pass exactly one of value or reset: true. The result reports applied and previous values plus a restore receipt. The value read before the first change is kept; in a daemon session, release or rebind restores every sensor the session changed. Sessionless changes persist until reset. Physical devices and iOS are refused. Read current values with getDeviceState include: ["sensors"].

sensor.description: Emulator sensor. Three values (x:y:z): acceleration m/s² ±1000, gyroscope rad/s ±100, magnetic-field µT ±2000; orientation azimuth 0..360, pitch -180..180, roll -90..90 degrees. One value: temperature °C -273.15..1000, proximity cm 0..100, light lux 0..200000, pressure hPa 0..2000, humidity % 0..100.

value.description: Value(s) to set, in the sensor's arity and range; rounded to 6 decimals.

reset.description: true restores the value read before the first setSensor change; use instead of value.

name: setToolEnabled
title: Set Tool Discovery
description: Control tools/list discovery for this MCP session: one exact name via toolName, or a batch via toolNames. name: terminateApp
title: Terminate App
description: Terminate app by package name

includeExtras.description: Opt in to raw accessibility extras metadata in structuredContent only (default off). Only meaningful with project:'full' or raw:true; text content always omits extras.

raw.description: Return the raw view hierarchy instead of the compact skeleton

project.description: Observation projection. 'skeleton' (default) returns a flat, actionable-only list (elementId/label/bounds/affordances) under `skeleton` in place of `viewHierarchy`; 'full' returns the raw view hierarchy under `viewHierarchy`. Each skeleton elementId/label is directly usable as a tapOn selector, except the collapsed keyboard row `<ime>` (drive it with sendKeys); re-request with raw/project:'full' to disambiguate.

skeleton.description: Always present alongside a diff (issue #6221 item 4.1): the same actionable-only selector surface a full observation's `skeleton` carries.

context.description: Non-actionable state-readout rows from the same projection as `skeleton` (issue #6221 item 1, #6256) — a timer countdown, a toggle's current-state text — present only when at least one such row survived. Populated alongside `skeleton` so a diff-mode response never silently drops the readout a client needs to tell a failed input from a successful one.

activeWindow.description: Same name/shape as a full observation's `activeWindow` (issue #6258): a diff-mode response otherwise carries no `activeWindow` at all, leaving a client no single accessor for 'what screen am I on' across full and diff modes. Populated from the post-transition observation, not by `diffObserveResult` itself.

freshness.description: Same name/shape as a full observation's `freshness` (issue #6258): a diff-mode response otherwise carries no `freshness` at all, leaving a client no single accessor for 'is this capture fresh' across full and diff modes. Populated from the post-transition observation, not by `diffObserveResult` itself.

screenSize.description: Same platform-native coordinate space as a full observation's `screenSize` and hierarchy/skeleton bounds; `units` identifies that space when present. Populated from the post-action observation, not by `diffObserveResult` itself.

truncationReasons.description: Why the captured hierarchy is incomplete (issue #6601) — the same field a full observation carries, so a client reads it the same way in both modes. In diff mode (issue #6933), any reason — host-cap (max_children[...]) or capture-fidelity (max_nodes, max_depth, max_children, cancelled) — may originate from either comparison input (baseline or current capture), so its presence means the comparison may be incomplete, not that this diff's own `skeleton`/`context` omit rows.

settled.description: Same name/meaning as a full observation's `settled` (issue #6866): whether the observation this diff was computed from passed the hierarchy-stability gate. Populated from the post-action observation, not by `diffObserveResult` itself, so a diff-mode client has the same accessor as a full-mode one.

settleMs.description: Same name/meaning as a full observation's `settleMs` (issue #9591), copied from the post-action observation.

settlePolls.description: Same name/meaning as a full observation's `settlePolls` (issue #9591), copied from the post-action observation.

accessibilityAuditSkipped.description: Same name/meaning as a full observation's `accessibilityAuditSkipped` (issue #6926): `settled_capture_adopted` means a settled capture replaced the action's original capture, so its audit was deliberately dropped rather than mismatched onto the returned hierarchy.

added.description: Absent on action-observation diffs: the diff's `skeleton` already lists every actionable node on the current screen (#11637).

removed.description: Absent on action-observation diffs: the diff's `skeleton` already lists every actionable node on the current screen (#11637).

key.description: INTERNAL positional identity key — see observeDiffNodeSchema.key. NOT a selector.

fromKey.description: The node's INTERNAL key on the baseline side, present only on content-identity re-pairs.

selector.description: Real, tapOn-usable selector for this diff entry, when one could be derived from its resource-id/view-id/text/content-desc — the same vocabulary skeleton rows use. Prefer this over `key` (issue #6221 item 4).

elementId.description: Android synthetic s2- ids are valid only for the observation that returned them; re-observe after the screen changes.

index.description: Replay disambiguator from the next observation's skeleton for a repeated elementId or id-less label. Omitted when the node is absent or its own group contains a promotable inert match. Unique selectors carry neither index nor ambiguous.

ambiguous.description: True when this selector matches multiple candidates, including inert nodes, and a safe replay index cannot be emitted. Never present with index or on a unique selector.

backend.description: iOS only, when the app registered an AutoMobile SDK observation bridge: sdk when its nodes were used, xctest when XCTest stood in.

fallbackReason.description: Why XCTest stood in for the bridge: it did not answer, or it does not support the action.

hierarchyServiceStarted.description: Present only when this session-less read started the hierarchy service on an unowned device.

truncationReasons.description: Per-window capture truncation codes (max_nodes, max_depth, max_children, cancelled, or newer APK codes). Absent or null when unavailable; complete windows omit reasons. Full/raw output keeps these here.

anyOf.description: Compact bounds tuple [left, top, right, bottom].

truncationReasons.description: Why the captured hierarchy is incomplete (issue #6601). Present only when rows were dropped — a device-side stop (max_nodes, max_depth, max_children, cancelled) or the host per-node child cap (max_children[<node> kept N of M]). This is the nested location `sanitizeObserveResult` leaves raw hierarchy reasons under `project:"full"` or `raw:true`; capture-fidelity reasons may also be lifted to the top-level `truncationReasons` field for skeleton/diff output, while a host-output max_children cap is not lifted to a non-diff skeleton.

Why the captured hierarchy is incomplete (issue #6601) — the same field a diff-mode observation carries, so a client reads it the same way in both modes. On this non-diff arm, it contains only capture-fidelity reasons (device-side max_nodes, max_depth, max_children, cancelled); its presence means `skeleton`/`context` omit rows. A host-output max_children[<node> kept N of M] cap trims only rendered `viewHierarchy` and is not lifted here.

settled.description: Whether this observation passed the hierarchy-stability gate (issue #6866): two consecutive structurally-equal captures. `false` means the bound expired, the action was not navigation-class, or the action failed — in every case the capture was never confirmed stable. Stamped on every embedded action observation.

settleMs.description: Milliseconds the hierarchy-stability gate spent re-observing (issue #9591). Present only when the gate ran. With `settled: false`, a value near the gate's budget means the screen kept changing or each read was slow; a value well below it means the gate stopped early.

settlePolls.description: Re-observations the hierarchy-stability gate took (issue #9591). Two are needed to settle; fewer at the budget means reads were too slow to compare.

accessibilityAuditSkipped.description: Why a requested accessibility audit was omitted from this observation (issue #6926): `settled_capture_adopted` means a settled capture replaced the action's original capture, so its audit was deliberately dropped rather than mismatched onto the returned hierarchy.

name: uninstallApp
title: Uninstall App
description: Uninstall app by package name or bundle identifier

keepData.description: Keep app data after uninstall (Android only, default false)

expectedSigningSha256.description: Android: complete signer set (SHA-256 of every signing certificate) the installed package must have; a different signer set, absence, or signers that cannot be read refuses the uninstall, and removal is confirmed by a fresh presence read.

name: videoRecording
title: Record Video
description: Start or stop device video recording. resourceLink on stop links its full result; required fields stay inline, bounded.

audio.description: Also record the device's audio into the file (start only; local emulators and iOS Simulators; needs FFmpeg)

display.description: Android panel key, role, or "active" (start only)

resourceLink.description: Return the complete result as an automobile:tool-output resource and a resource_link block instead of inline (default off). Only the headline fields stay inline; read the link to get the rest.

name: wakeAndUnlock
title: Wake and Unlock
description: Wake a device and unlock its keyguard. Android: swipe lock or secure PIN via `pin`; iOS: wake + swipe-dismiss (pin ignored).

pin.description: Credential to unlock a secure Android device. Optional; logically required to unlock a secure lock unless a pin was already remembered this session. Ignored on iOS.

name: windowMode
title: Set Window Mode
description: Android: put an app's task into fullscreen, picture-in-picture (enter via HOME; the app must support PiP), freeform (optional bounds) or split screen with a second app, and read the mode and bounds back. Returns a restore receipt for the previous mode and any freeform settings it turned on. observe reports each task's windowingMode and bounds in backStack.tasks.

appId.description: Package whose task to move

mode.description: "fullscreen"; {pip: enter|exit}; {freeform: {bounds?}} (turns on freeform settings, receipted); {splitScreen: {with?, position?}}

bounds.description: Window bounds in display pixels

with.description: Second app's package; required on API 32+

restore.description: A returned restore receipt: puts the window back, then the settings. Same boot only
